extracted.intended_audience: regulatory commenters, agency staff, administrative law scholars, public-interest advocates
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting public comments to administrative agencies that are useful, navigable, and resistant to industry 'information capture' tactics; focuses on the structure, timing, and methodological transparency of comments submitted during notice-and-comment rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information capture tactics (what to recognize and counter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics regulated industry uses to capture rulemaking by overwhelming or obscuring: volume dumps; complexity escalation; strategic late filings; information silos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that 'volume dumps' (thousands of pages), 'complexity escalation' (highly specialized models and jargon), 'strategic late filings' (submitting key analyses near the close), and 'information silos' (releasing data only within favorable comment packages) are strategies that impede agency processing and can capture the record. Comments and agency procedures should anticipate and neutralize these tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the comment navigable (executive summary, table of contents, plain-language overview)?
rubrics_metrics.description: A good comment is navigable rather than maximally voluminous: it should include an executive summary, organizational aids, and plain-language explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a short executive summary stating the key requested change, a table of contents or index to appendices, and plain-language overviews of technical material so agency staff can quickly grasp the core arguments without parsing technical appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a short executive summary with the key requested change
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment should open with a concise executive summary that highlights the requested change or principal argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive summaries allow agencies to identify the core position fast; make the requested regulatory action explicit and summarize the primary supporting reasons and evidence in a few clear paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index appendices and technical material clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize and index appendices and technical attachments so reviewers can locate supporting data and analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear table of contents, labeled appendices, and cross-references in the text. Avoid burying critical evidence deep in unattributed or unlabeled files; signal where each piece of evidence lives and what it supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide plain-language translations of technical analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate technical methods, models, and results into accessible, plain-language summaries that non-specialist agency reviewers can understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize key assumptions, mechanisms, and implications in everyday language; use figures or simple tables where helpful. Do not rely solely on opaque technical files to make your case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose underlying data, models, and assumptions transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should disclose the data sources, modeling approaches, and assumptions used to generate analyses and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List datasets, provide citations to public sources, document model specifications, and explain key assumptions. When possible, provide access to data or URLs so agency staff or third parties can inspect the inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reproducible methods rather than black-box analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical methods should be reproducible by the agency or third parties instead of opaque or proprietary black boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail (or code and data) so others can rerun the analysis; avoid submitting results without the means for verification. If proprietary methods are used, explain them or provide alternative reproducible demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite publicly available sources and provide reproducibility paths
rubrics_metrics.description: Support assertions with citations to publicly available literature, data, and documentation, and indicate how the agency can reproduce results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full citations, data repositories, methodological appendices, and, where feasible, scripts or step-by-step instructions to replicate analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and challenge undisclosed assumptions in opposing submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A useful comment calls out hidden or undisclosed assumptions in industry or opposing comments and explains their implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify assumptions that materially affect conclusions (e.g., baseline parameters, discount rates, model functional forms), show how alternative assumptions change results, and discuss why undisclosed assumptions undermine the credibility of opposing analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-run industry models with different assumptions and report differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Counteract industry capture by reanalyzing industry-provided models under alternative, transparent assumptions and reporting the variance in outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where industry submits a model, attempt to replicate it and then change key assumptions to show robustness (or lack thereof). Document differences clearly and explain their regulatory significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make proprietary data demands of the agency or industry
rubrics_metrics.description: When critical analyses rely on proprietary or undisclosed data, commenters should press for disclosure or for agencies to obtain necessary underlying data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request the agency insist on access to underlying data or provide public alternatives; explain why proprietary opacity prevents meaningful review and suggest remedies (e.g., data deposition, redaction protocols).

rubrics_metrics.name: File at ANPRM stage or early in the comment period when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments early (ideally at the Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking stage) so the agency has time to digest substantive material rather than receiving it as a late dump.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early filing allows agencies to incorporate feedback into rule proposals and reduces the effectiveness of late strategic filings. If filing later, avoid last-minute volume dumps; signal major submissions in advance and summarize late material succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid contributing to filter failure by being targeted, not a volume dump
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should aim to be targeted and helpful rather than maximally voluminous; excessive length can worsen agency filter failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize the clearest, most relevant evidence and analysis. Use appendices for detailed material but ensure the main comment is focused. Over-large submissions that are poorly organized can be functionally invisible to busy agency staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Was the comment filed early enough for agency processing?
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing matters: assess whether the submission was made early enough to be meaningfully processed by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the comment was filed during ANPRM or early in the comment period; late strategic filings are more likely to overwhelm or evade agency consideration.
